ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in Figure 1, an inclined conveyor belt makes an angle of $37^{\circ}$ with the horizontal ground, and the conveyor belt rotates counterclockwise at a constant speed. Now, an object with a mass of 1 kg is released from rest at point A at the top of the conveyor belt and slides off the conveyor belt after 2s. The v-t graph of the object's motion on the conveyor belt is shown in Figure 2. The object can be regarded as a point mass, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. What is the distance from the top A to the bottom B of the conveyor belt?
2. What are the magnitude and direction of the frictional force during the time interval $1\!\sim\!2\mathbf{s}$?
3. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the conveyor belt?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
16m
4N, direction upward along the conveyor belt
0.5

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure 1 in the figure shows an inclined conveyor belt, the upper right end is marked as A, the lower left end is marked as B, the angle between the conveyor belt and the horizontal dashed line is 37°, the rotation direction of the belt wheel is marked with arrows, and the block is located on the inclined conveyor belt. Figure 2 is the graph of the block's velocity v versus time t: the broken line starts from (0 s, 0 m/s), goes to (1 s, 10 m/s), then to (2 s, 12 m/s), and t=1 s, t=2 s as well as v=10 m/s, v=12 m/s are marked with dashed lines. Reasoning: Take the direction in which the block moves downward along the conveyor belt from A to B as the positive direction. The displacement of the block on the conveyor belt is equal to the area under the v-t graph. The area from 0～1 s is a triangle: S1 = 1/2 × 1 × 10 = 5 m; the area from 1～2 s is a trapezoid: S2 = (10 + 12)/2 × 1 = 11 m. Therefore the length of the conveyor belt from A to B is S = 5 + 11 = 16 m. During 1～2 s, the slope of the v-t graph is a = (12 - 10)/(2 - 1) = 2 m/s^2, with direction downward along the conveyor belt. Forces along the inclined-plane direction: the gravitational component mg sin37° is downward, and the friction force in this stage is upward, so mg sin37° - f = ma. Substituting m=1 kg, g=10 m/s^2, sin37°=0.6, gives 6 - f = 2, so f = 4 N, with direction upward along the conveyor belt. The supporting force N = mg cos37° = 1 × 10 × 0.8 = 8 N. The kinetic friction force f = μN, so μ = f/N = 4/8 = 0.5.
